title: Cause and effect: why things happen
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Things happen for reasons. The cause is WHY something happens; the effect is WHAT happens as a result. Spotting them helps you follow any text. Quick words: cause means the reason why something happens. effect means what happens because of the cause.
The cause is why something happens. The effect is what happens as a result.

steps: 'It rained heavily.' — this is the cause.
'So the match was cancelled.' — this is the effect.
Signal words like because, so and since often link them.

blocks.question: In 'She studied hard, so she passed the test', what is the EFFECT?
blocks.explain: Passing the test is what happened as a result, so it is the effect.
blocks.rule: The cause is why something happens; the effect is what happens as a result.

practiceItems.prompt: the reason something happens is the ___
what happens as a result is the ___
in 'it rained so we stayed in', the cause is the ___
in 'he tripped and fell', the effect is that he ___

blocks.content: Signal words help you spot cause and effect: because, so, since, therefore, as a result.

blocks.question: Which word signals a cause?
blocks.rule: Signal words like because, so, since and therefore link a cause to its effect.

practiceItems.prompt: a signal word that introduces a reason
a signal word that introduces a result
cause and effect are linked by signal ___

blocks.question: 'The road was icy, so the car slid.' What is the cause and what is the effect?
options: Cause: the icy road; effect: the car slid
Cause: the car slid; effect: the icy road
blocks.explain: The cause is the reason something happens; the effect is what results. The icy road came first and made the car slide, so the icy road is the cause and the sliding is the effect. The word 'so' points to the effect.
blocks.rule: The cause happens first and makes the effect; 'so' often signals the effect.
blocks.principle: Cause and effect are linked in order: reason then result.

rubric.look_for: names the icy road as cause, sliding as effect

misconceptions.coach: The road iced over first, then the car slid — cause then effect.
'so' connects the cause to its effect.

practiceItems.prompt: the reason something happens is the
what happens as a result is the
in 'icy road, so car slid', the cause is the
the word that often signals an effect

blocks.content: Ask 'why did it happen?' for the cause, and 'what happened?' for the effect. Watch for because and so. Let's practise!
